reviews.review:
Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine is a linear third person shooter with hack and slash mechanics blended into it. We play as Captain Titus of the Ultramarine who is accompanied by two other Ultramarine subordinates to fight back against an ork invasion on a forge planet in order to retrieve the Inquisitor and get off world with him safely. However things don't always go according to plan....

There is a decent variety of weapons that we would come across as we advance through the chapters ranging from plasma pistols to bolter rifles and heavy machine guns. We are able to carry up to 4 different weapons so you can switch accordingly to different enemy threats. Ammo and grenade refill boxes are scattered around the levels, so ammo is not an issue in this game. Health on the other hand might be a problem especially on the harder difficulty since there is no health pack and the only way to regain health is to either do a finishing move on an enemy or activated fury mode which is not always available.

Unlike most other games that utilize skill points for upgrades, upgrades in this game are aquired from pods scattered through the levels. There is a fury mode that can enhanced both melee and ranged weapon attacks for a certain duration (Fury is gained through killing enemies). There is a decent variety of enemy types for both the Ork enemies in the first half of the game and the Chaos enemies in the second half which is commendable. There are also collectibles in the form of servo skulls that would provide some audio lore to the game's universe.

Besides the Single Player campaign, there is also a co-op mode in the form of "exterminatus" which is basically horde mode with a certain number of enemies waves that you need to survive. There is also a PVP mode with the fairly generic "capture the flag", "Domination", "Team vs Team" and so on. More customization options can be unlocked as you play more of them to increase player levels. Suprisingly there are still people playing the multiplayer mode as I was able to find a match fairly quickly. (less than a min)

Overall, I think Warhammer 40,00: space marine is pretty decent in terms of story and gameplay. However the ending is pretty disappointing as the final boss is basically a QTE fight and it ends with a cliffhanger which would leave you with many questions in regards to the story. The lack of cover based mechanic is also pretty weird as this game would certainly benefit from it instead of awkwardly trying to hide behind cover by standing behind it. I give this game a 6/10!
